record.paper_title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
record.original_question: For each of the 47 planar rational systems among the non-single-equation group of 300 special cases that may be competitive for some parameter ranges and are nowhere cooperative, determine whether the competitive-system monotonicity hypotheses corresponding to Theorem 3.12 or Theorem 3.13 hold, and then determine the global behavior of all solutions. The 47 systems are (14,l), (15,l), and (29,l) with l in {30,35,36,43,45,47,48,49}; (30,l) with l in {30,35,36,38,43,45,47,48,49}; (35,38), (35,43), (36,38), (36,43); and (38,l), (43,l) with l in {43,45,47,48,49}. The relevant Theorem 3.12 hypothesis is that a one-step simultaneous decrease or simultaneous increase of both components forces the same direction in the previous step, yielding eventual monotonicity of both component sequences; the relevant Theorem 3.13 hypothesis is the analogous two-step condition yielding eventual monotonicity of the four even and odd component subsequences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider planar rational difference systems of the form
\[
 x_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha_1 + \beta_1 x_n + \gamma_1 y_n}{A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n}, \qquad y_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha_2 + \beta_2 x_n + \gamma_2 y_n}{A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n},
\]
where all parameters are nonnegative reals (with denominators positive on the relevant invariant region of $[0,\infty)^2$), and where each of the two equations is chosen from the finite list of normalized rational forms obtained by taking subsets of the terms $\{1,x,y\}$ in numerator and denominator (yielding a finite catalogue of system types indexed by pairs $(k,l)$ of equation labels).

Call a map $T:(x,y)\mapsto(f(x,y),g(x,y))$ on a rectangular region of $[0,\infty)^2$ \emph{competitive} if $f$ is nondecreasing in $x$ and nonincreasing in $y$, and $g$ is nonincreasing in $x$ and nondecreasing in $y$; call it \emph{cooperative} if $f,g$ are both nondecreasing in each variable. Consider the following two monotonicity criteria for a competitive map $T$ and its iterates $(x_n,y_n)=T^n(x_0,y_0)$:

(H1) For every orbit, whenever both $x_{n+1}\le x_n$ and $y_{n+1}\le y_n$ (resp.\ $\ge$) occur at some step, the same simultaneous inequalities held at the previous step. Under (H1) both sequences $\{x_n\}$ and $\{y_n\}$ are eventually monotonic.

(H2) The analogous two-step condition: whenever simultaneous weak inequalities of the two components occur at step $n+1$, they held at step $n-1$. Under (H2) the four subsequences $\{x_{2n}\},\{x_{2n+1}\},\{y_{2n}\},\{y_{2n+1}\}$ are eventually monotonic.

Now restrict to the following 47 system types (labelled by index pairs $(k,l)$ from the catalogue) which are known to be competitive on some nonempty parameter region and which are nowhere cooperative:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(14,l),\ (15,l),\ (29,l)\ \text{for } l\in\{30,35,36,43,45,47,48,49\};\\
&(30,l)\ \text{for } l\in\{30,35,36,38,43,45,47,48,49\};\\
&(35,38),\ (35,43),\ (36,38),\ (36,43);\\
&(38,l),\ (43,l)\ \text{for } l\in\{43,45,47,48,49\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For each such system, and for each parameter subregion on which the system is competitive on a forward-invariant rectangle:

(a) Determine whether hypothesis (H1) holds (so that every orbit has eventually monotone components), or whether (H2) holds (so that the even- and odd-indexed subsequences are eventually monotone).

(b) Using such monotonicity, together with boundedness/invariance analysis, classify the global asymptotic behavior of every solution with initial condition in the invariant region: identify all fixed points and period-two points, their local stability, the basins of attraction, and the limiting behavior (convergence to an equilibrium, to a period-two cycle, or escape) of every orbit.
artifact.status_search_result: A search did not surface a definitive resolution of this collection of open problems concerning the 47 partially competitive planar rational systems; subsequent literature on global behavior of planar rational systems treats individual cases but no comprehensive solution covering all 47 systems was located.
